summary: Intermittent SSE gap during auth token refresh window causes truncated final sentences and duplicate metadata
description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasDocs reported intermittent truncation of SSE streaming responses during a multi-minute window following an auth token refresh. The client observed the final sentence of generated responses occasionally missing and, in several cases, a duplicated metadata envelope (system messages / role attributes) inserted midstream after the client reconnected.

Impact:
- Affects a subset of production users of AtlasDocs in us-east using SSE for long-running generation.
- Truncated paragraphs lead to malformed documents in their ingestion pipeline; business impact: downstream docs missing closing paragraphs causing parsing errors.
- Intermittent, reproducible within token refresh scenario; not all streams are affected.

Environment:
- Production (us-east), hosted Redwood API endpoint behind edge-proxy + ALB.
- AtlasDocs is enterprise plan with pinned model redwood-llama-70b.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Start a long SSE generation with a conversation prompt (typical length 800-1500 tokens).
2) Let generation run until auth token rotation window (customer client configured to refresh tokens proactively around 55m).
3) Token refresh triggers an SSE reconnect path on the client; sometimes client attempts resume, sometimes full reconnect.
4) Observe the final 1-3 sentences of the response missing or the stream contains a repeated metadata envelope followed by a truncated tail.

Observed behavior:
- Server-side logs show a complete final chunk emitted for the generation id, but client-side captures show either a gap (no final tokens) or a duplicate metadata event inserted before the final tokens, effectively making the final tokens be dropped by the client parser.
- In metrics, a small spike in 5xx/stream-timeout correlates with the affected windows.
- Reconnect path varies by client SDK version; older SDKs more likely to fall back to full reconnect.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should stitch tokens idempotently without duplication and without losing the closing tokens.
- If client fully reconnects, server should send a consistent snapshot/resume payload that preserves the final tokens or include an explicit terminal marker.

Attachments / evidence:
- Customer-provided browser HAR and a trimmed SSE transcript (attached to ticket).
- Server trace snippets showing final emit at 2026-03-10T18:32:15Z for convo id conv_9a1b and subsequent ACK window logs.
- Grafana snapshots of stream success rate and auth rotation events in the 5-minute window.

Notes about scope:
- This appears specific to the interplay between token refresh, edge connection handoff, and our resume id mapping and is distinct from simple proxy truncation (we have separate tickets for ALB half-close patterns).

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge rebind + token rotation leads to resume id mismatch. The server accepts the new session but our resume id mapping may point to a stale snapshot when rebind occurs during inflight streaming KV priming.

Hypothesis 2: Client parser behavior: when a metadata envelope appears midstream, older SDKs treat it as a message boundary and drop following tokens if ordering differs. New SDK includes a more tolerant parser.

Evidence: Server traces show final token batch emitted but the corresponding ACK window not observed from client prior to disconnect. Edge logs show connection handoff between two proxies within 500-1200ms of token refresh request.

Reproduction: Added test harness that simulates token refresh and randomized edge rebind; reproduced truncation consistently when rebind happened within 1.5s of resume window. Patch candidate simulated resolved the case in unit/integration tests.

Risk assessment: Patch small and scoped (resume id grace window + ordered ack handshake). Potential side-effect: slightly extended time where resume id is considered canonical (5s) — low risk for correctness, small additional state retention needed on edge nodes.
Related: PRs and runbooks linked; see github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4321 for code changes and confluence page for design notes.
resolution: Mitigation deployed (2026-03-12): v1.8.3 of serving-runtime plus edge proxy config change rolled to us-east. Changes: (1) 5s resume-id grace window after auth refresh, (2) ordered-ack handshake on resume envelopes, (3) additional logging on resume mismatch cases.

Customer remediation: AtlasDocs upgraded client SDK to v2.4.1 and added a 3s random jitter to token refresh timing. They reported a significant drop in truncation occurrences in staging and early production sampling.

Verification: Post-deploy metrics show affected stream error rate in us-east decreased from ~1.2% to 0.03% in the 48h window. No new regressions observed in perf dashboards. Extended monitoring scheduled for 7 days.

Follow-ups: (1) Add an automated integration test that exercises token refresh + edge rebind scenarios in CI. (2) Update streaming SDK docs with recommended token refresh jitter and fallback guidance. (3) Schedule a postmortem and update public runbook if outage threshold crossed. Postmortem draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Stream+Auth+Rotation+Postmortem (in progress).
Status: Monitoring — leaving ticket open until 2026-03-19 for confirmation; will close if no recurrence and AtlasDocs signs off.
